claim.pdf_says: The 10.6.1 COBOL compilation group general format prints the repetition ellipsis INSIDE the outer bracket, immediately to the right of the closing brace: [ { program-prototype / function-prototype / program-definition / function-definition / class-definition / interface-definition } … ]  — the '…' glyph sits between the closing brace and the closing bracket (verified at 300 dpi; the closing bracket's right stroke is clearly to the right of the ellipsis).
claim.markdown_says:
```
⎡ ⎧ program-prototype    ⎫ ⎤
⎢ ⎪ function-prototype   ⎪ ⎥
⎢ ⎨ program-definition   ⎬ ⎥ …
⎢ ⎪ function-definition  ⎪ ⎥
⎢ ⎪ class-definition     ⎪ ⎥
⎣ ⎩ interface-definition ⎭ ⎦
```

> **Figure notes (COBOL compilation group general format syntax diagram).** … the `…` immediately to the right of the bracket pair repeats the whole bracketed portion, so a compilation group is zero or more source units in any mix.
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.7 the ellipsis binds to the delimiter immediately to its LEFT. In the printed standard it binds to the BRACE (repeat the chosen source-unit selection) and the whole repeated group is then optional; the markdown moved it outside the bracket so it binds to the BRACKET, and the figure note then asserts that wrong binding as if it were the standard's. Any grammar or doc derived from the markdown records the wrong nesting of repetition vs. optionality for the top-level compilation-group production.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent pixel measurement of the 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v286/spec_p286.png, 2550x3300). Both sources were quoted accurately; neither is misquoted, and this is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture.

Geometry of the printed 10.6.1 figure, measured in the band y=750..1160 by thresholding at 128 and locating full-height vertical strokes:
  x=273-274  vertical stroke spanning y 773..1130, serifs extending RIGHT at the bottom row (row 1130 ink at x 273..288)  ->  OUTER OPENING BRACKET '['
  x=311-312  brace spine (h~325)                                                                                        ->  opening brace '{'
  x=757-758  brace spine (h~325), cusp ink at x 760..766 centred on y 942..951                                          ->  closing brace '}'
  x=792-795, 801-804, 810-813  three separate dot clusters on rows y 955..959                                           ->  the ELLIPSIS '…'
  x=831-832  vertical stroke spanning y 773..1130, serifs extending LEFT at both ends (row 1130 ink at x 819..832)      ->  OUTER CLOSING BRACKET ']'

Ordering is therefore closing brace (758) < ellipsis (792-813) < closing bracket (831). A scan of the whole figure band strictly to the RIGHT of the outer closing bracket (columns 835..1400) returns ZERO dark pixels, so nothing whatsoever is printed outside the bracket. The only ink between the closing brace and the closing bracket is the brace cusp and the three ellipsis dots. The printed general format is unambiguously:

    [ { program-prototype | function-prototype | program-definition | function-definition | class-definition | interface-definition } … ]

The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 12431 ff.) instead prints '…' on the middle row AFTER the '⎥' bracket segment, i.e. outside the outer closing bracket. That is a genuine mis-transcription of a NORMATIVE general-format diagram, and the accompanying figure note compounds it by asserting as fact something the printed page contradicts: it says 'the `…` immediately to the right of the bracket pair repeats the whole bracketed portion', whereas on the printed page the '…' is immediately to the right of the BRACE pair and inside the bracket. The transcription elsewhere tracks exactly this inside/outside distinction deliberately and explicitly (e.g. the Function-identifier note 'the ellipsis sits **inside** the parentheses', the report section note 'the ellipsis **outside** the closing bracket', the varying-phrase note, and the INVOKE USING note 'the ellipsis is INSIDE those brackets'), so the placement is a tracked content property of these figures, not incidental layout — and here it is recorded backwards.

The claim's citation of the binding rule is also correct: the metalanguage rule (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2705) states that given an ellipsis, one scans right to left for the right bracket or right brace delimiter immediately to its left, finds the logically matching left delimiter, and the ellipsis applies to the portion between that pair. Applied to the printed form the ellipsis binds to the BRACE group; applied to the markdown form it binds to the BRACKET group. Different binding, different recorded nesting — so the claim is real.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, and the location and quotations are exactly right, but the stated consequence is overstated and the severity should be downgraded from 'structural' to 'figure-fidelity / note-is-wrong'.

What is genuinely wrong: (1) the markdown places the repetition ellipsis outside the outer closing bracket when the printed standard places it inside, immediately right of the closing brace; (2) the editorial figure note affirmatively misdescribes the printed page, claiming the '…' is 'immediately to the right of the bracket pair'. Fix by moving the '…' inside the bracket column (so the middle row reads '⎢ ⎨ program-definition   ⎬ … ⎥') and rewriting the note to say the ellipsis applies to the BRACE pair — each repetition selects exactly one of the six source-unit kinds — with the enclosing bracket then making the whole repeated group optional.

Where the claim overreaches: it asserts the two nestings record different grammar. They do not generate different languages here. Printed '[ {choice} … ]' = optional(one-or-more choices) = zero or more source units; the markdown's '[ {choice} ] …' = one-or-more of (optional choice) = also zero or more source units. Both collapse to the same production, and the note's own concluding sentence ('a compilation group is zero or more source units in any mix') is therefore correct despite reaching it by the wrong route. So a grammar derived from the markdown would NOT be wrong for the compilation-group production; the defect is that a normative diagram is transcribed inaccurately and its note states a falsehood about the printed standard, which is a transcription-fidelity defect rather than a semantic one.
